sections.name: CREATE
sections.title: Creates data tables and indexes
sections.what: Creates a table for each kind of record, such as cases, documents, parcels, verification results and anchor events. Most tables store their details as one text payload tied to a case ID. The anchor events table stores fingerprints and the signer, and allows only one anchor per subject. Indexes speed up lookups by case. The end of this section starts a rule function that the next section finishes.
sections.why: Likely reason: each table is created only if missing, so the script can be run again safely.
sections.watch_out: Because most details are stored as text, the database cannot check their contents, so bad data will not be caught here.

sections.name: BEGIN
sections.title: Rule that blocks changes to anchors
sections.what: Finishes a database function that raises an error with the message that anchor events are append-only, meaning they can be added but not changed or removed.
sections.why: Likely reason: anchored fingerprints are meant to be a permanent record, so the database itself refuses edits.
sections.watch_out: Only ordinary changes are blocked. A database administrator who disables the trigger can still edit anchors, and a wrong anchor cannot be corrected by normal means.

sections.name: CREATE
sections.title: Attaches the rule to anchor events
sections.what: Adds a trigger to the anchor events table so every update or delete calls the rule. It is added only if a trigger with that name does not already exist.
sections.why: Likely reason: prevents the trigger from being added twice when the script is run again.
sections.watch_out: The check looks only at the trigger name, so if someone changes the trigger by hand, running the script again will not restore it.

summary: Database setup script that creates the data tables and makes anchor records permanent.
purpose: Creates the tables the app uses and locks anchor events against changes.
why: Likely reason: anchor records act as proof, so they must not be altered after they are saved.
how: First, the script creates each table and its indexes only if they are missing. Then it defines a rule that rejects any update or delete. Last, it attaches that rule to the anchor events table, but only if it is not already attached.
inputs: Run in the Supabase SQL editor. It takes no inputs.
outputs: Database tables, indexes, a rule function and a trigger.
risks: The trigger protects only anchor events. Most tables store details as unchecked text. No foreign keys link records to cases, so related rows are not enforced.
debug: If an edit to anchor events fails, that is the intended rule. If an anchor must be corrected, an administrator has to handle the trigger. If a table is missing, run the script again.
